label: diffuse token-identity unit: p/b/2/w inputs (original) or e/x/v/h outputs (copy)
explanation: Dense, broadly distributed unit (5% of steps, 39% of sequences) with no capturable rule. Original phase (58% of mass): never at t=0, highest rate at t=1-2; enriched for inputs p, b, 2, w (about 2.5-2.9x lift) and previous inputs q, p, b. Runs of these tokens in a row raise precision to about 0.5 but recall drops to about 0.2. Copy phase (40% of mass): enriched when the token being output is e, x, v or h (about 3.5x), with weaker lift for m and n. It rarely fires at the delimiter or on the first two copy outputs. The best union of the two clauses gets dev F1 0.32 (precision 0.23, recall 0.51, mass recall 0.60), and adding more conditions did not improve it. It behaves like a superposed token-identity direction, not a monosemantic feature. Magnitude rises somewhat with L (L=9 has 1.2x the rate), but no clean magnitude driver was found.
